I am 70 years old this year, and I have been working these fields since I was 20. I only went to primary school for a few years — enough to count money and read the numbers on a fertilizer bag, but that is all. My husband passed away 15 years ago. Now my two sons work in Shijiazhuang and send money home, and my daughter-in-law helps when the busy seasons come. We have 18 mu of land altogether, which is a lot for an old woman, but I manage.

I do not start from nothing each year. I start from what I did last year, and I adjust only a little. Last year was decent, so this year I will do mostly the same. I have 10 mu that I do wheat and corn on — plant wheat in October, harvest in June, then plant corn right after. The other 8 mu I keep for cotton. Cotton earns good money when the price holds, but it is heavy work with all the spraying.

**Wheat:** I rotary till the 10 mu after the corn comes off, then sow in early October. I use improved seed, about 30 jin per mu. For fertilizer, I put down one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu as my base — 100 jin of the 15-15-15 general kind. Then in March when the wheat greens up, I spread another 100 jin of ammonium bicarbonate per mu on top. That is what my neighbor Old Wang does, and his wheat always looks greener than mine if I skip it. I would rather put on a bit too much than risk a thin crop — fertilizer is money, but a bad harvest is a disaster. I irrigate four times from the well: once before winter freeze, twice in spring, and once at grain filling. I spray insecticide twice, herbicide once, and fungicide once — four times total. I expect about 900 jin per mu this year if the spring rain comes.

**Maize:** After we harvest the wheat in June, I do not till again — too hot and too much work. I plant the hybrid corn seed directly into the stubble, about 1 package per mu. I put down 80 jin per mu of high-nitrogen compound fertilizer at sowing — the special corn formula. I do not topdress; by mid-summer I am too busy with the cotton and my legs hurt in the heat. I irrigate twice, at the big trumpet stage and at filling. I spray insecticide twice and herbicide once. I should get around 1000 jin per mu.

**Cotton:** I rotary till the 8 mu in late April. I plant improved cotton seed, about 3 jin per mu. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base — 100 jin of 15-15-15. When flowering starts, I add another 50 jin per mu of compound fertilizer. Cotton is the reason I cannot sleep at night — it needs spraying all the time. I spray insecticide 15 times for bollworms and aphids, fungicide 4 times, and I use growth regulator twice. I also weed by hand and machine. I irrigate three times. Last year I got about 700 jin of seed cotton per mu. I hope for the same.

My sons tell me I use too much fertilizer and that the government says to cut back. But I saw what happened to Old Li two years ago when he tried to save 30 yuan per mu on fertilizer — his wheat came up short and thin, and he lost hundreds. I will not make that mistake. Every jin of fertilizer I put down is insurance against hunger.
